newsitem.title: POLAND: Bank group sets conditions for Polish shipyard.
newsitem.headline: Bank group sets conditions for Polish shipyard.

text.p: Polish banks interested in financing the construction of five ships for a German client by the New Gdansk Shipyard have set four conditions under which they would credit the deal, one of the banks said on Monday.

The leader of the seven-bank consortium, Bank Gdanski SA, said in a statement that the group wanted the New Gdansk yard to boost its capital, because government guarantees did not cover the full scope of the loan.

They also want the yard to re-negotiate deadlines for the first two ships and insist that the contracts for the construction of the ships be transferred from the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard to the new yard.
Finally, banks demand a realistic plan of changes in the functioning and organisation of the bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard.

The yard, the cradle of the Solidarity movement which overthrew communism in 1989, was declared bankrupt last year after its debts reached 415 million zlotys and banks refused to credit its further operation.
Because the yard still had unfilled orders, part of the shipyard's assets and workforce was moved to a newly-created, debt-free New Gdansk Shipyard to complete the contracts.

On January 15, the new yard signed a contract with Germany's Schoeller Holding Ltd for the construction of five container ships worth $27.5 million each, but still needs to win banks' confidence to get cash for their construction.
Gdanski said banks interested in participating in the consortium would decide whether to join it by February 15.
